answer: An agent market makes a locked bond its trust anchor: every identity, whether trading copper or forecasting a zephyr, must escrow 100 credits for 30 days to receive one job slot. The ledger prevents the same funds from backing multiple identities, and extra names earn no extra slots without extra bonds. An attacker seeking 1,000 simultaneous identities must immobilize 100,000 credits, paying the capital cost rather than merely generating keys.
